descripcion: The third conditional talks about an unreal past: if we had checked, we wouldn't have lost it. At B1 the goal is to build the form correctly for the first time and recognise it as the language of regret about the past.

filas: I would have called you sooner.

ejemplos.texto: If we had checked the address, we wouldn't have gotten lost.
If I had known, I would have called you.
We might have arrived on time if the train hadn't been delayed.

notas: The past perfect (had + participle) is used in the if-clause, and would have + participle in the main clause.
Would never appears inside the if-clause.
This structure is used only for a past that did not happen — both halves are unreal.

contraste.es: Spanish has an exact equivalent with si + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo and the conditional perfect (si hubiéramos revisado, no nos habríamos perdido), so the logic transfers directly.
contraste.de: German uses hätte in both halves (Wenn wir es geprüft hätten, hätten wir uns nicht verlaufen), which leads to If we had checked, we had not got lost. English needs had in the if-clause and would have in the result.
contraste.it: Italian has an exact equivalent (se avessimo controllato, non ci saremmo persi), so the logic transfers directly. In colloquial Italian the imperfetto sometimes replaces both halves (se controllavamo, non ci perdevamo), which can lead to if we checked, we didn't get lost.
contraste.fr: French has an exact equivalent (si nous avions vérifié, nous ne nous serions pas perdus), including the rule that the conditional never follows si. The logic and the form both transfer directly.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has an exact equivalent (se tivéssemos verificado, não nos teríamos perdido), so the logic transfers directly. In colloquial European Portuguese the result clause often uses tínhamos, which leads to we had not got lost instead of we wouldn't have got lost.

errores: Using would have in the if-clause.
Dropping have: if I had known, I would known.
Using the wrong participle: would have went instead of would have gone.

redemittel.expresion: If we had…, we wouldn't have…

traducciones.de: Wenn wir… hätten, hätten wir nicht…
traducciones.fr: Si nous avions…, nous n’aurions pas…
Cela ne serait pas arrivé si…

autochequeo: Is the if-clause in the past perfect, with no would?
Does the main clause use would have + participle correctly?
Have I built at least one complete third-conditional sentence?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the third conditional. Check for would inside the if-clause and check the participle forms in both parts of the sentence carefully. Do not rewrite the text.
